title: Deliver the reviewed design through CI, review, merge, and clean-room handoff

parentBehavior.description: Deliver one reviewed design prerequisite with explicit CI/review/merge ownership while keeping runtime and rollout as future gates.

problem: T003 has the complete feasibility, incident, replay, orphan, and rollout evidence, but the one-document delivery path, exact implementation finish line, clean-room handoff, and review-owned merge boundary still need one self-contained task packet.
outcome: The final task packet gives an independent reviewer one immutable design head to inspect, preserves the exact Current/Proposed contract and M-01–M-18 matrix, routes VAL-001 through its required read-only template, and stops the implementation workstation after the final head is pushed, the PR is open, required CI has started, and blocking feedback is addressed. Review owns terminal CI, conflicts, and merge; the Supervisor owns any later canary.
sourcePlanRef: factory/docs/operating-policy.md#validation-missions; #learning-and-controlled-change; #no-action-and-hold-policy; #executable-recovery-boundaries; requirement: reviewed merge precedes controlled rollout
actorAndTrigger: The planning/review owner receives dependency-ready T001–T003 evidence and prepares the final handoff. Validation receives only the immutable final head, acceptance rubric, public entry points, sanitized fixture, and budget. Review owns the PR's terminal checks, conflict resolution, and merge; the Portfolio Supervisor owns post-merge canary admission and promotion.
sharedSurfaceOwnership: T004 owns the final task packet and delivery handoff. No task may concurrently author the future design document. The future implementation owner owns production/API/generated/test changes; Recordings owns event append/replay; Automations owns classification/eligibility; Work/Factory Runtime owns public Work admission/move controls; build/release owns immutable YOU_TEST_BINARY; validation owns VAL-001; review owns terminal CI/conflicts/merge; the Portfolio Supervisor owns post-merge canary admission/promotion.

in: Additive reconciliation diagnostic result and controlled tabletop
Future unit, contract, functional, integration, and clean-room proof placement
One future design-document lease, exact owners, immutable artifact leases, commands, and unproven edges
PR, review, merge, and clean-room handoff ownership
One-session canary, observation window, hold, rollback, and promotion conditions
Security, privacy, performance, accessibility, localization, and cost boundaries
out: Generated files and executable test changes
Live event emission, live Factory settings, or active Work mutation
Canary execution, VAL-001 execution, terminal CI waiting, merge, and silent loopback repair

constraints: Factory Work and Factory Events remain the lifecycle authority; incident disposition is event metadata plus a replay-built projection, never a Work state, filesystem queue, or second store.
Preserve T001's ten-minute no-build/no-broad-test preflight and T002's reader-before-writer, same-ID payload equality, stable identity, and fail-closed partial-write rules.
Use Factory, Factory Session, Work, Worker Session, and Factory Event vocabulary; do not expose Petri-net implementation terminology in the future public design.
Routine design and implementation remain autonomous; do not invent an operator-approval Work.

The implementation-stage delivery criterion is exact: stop after the final head is pushed, the PR is open, CI has started, and blocking review feedback is addressed; do not poll or re-check CI after that finish line. Review owns terminal-and-passing CI, conflicts, and merge.
This iteration writes only the task artifacts plus untracked planner scaffolding; it does not create the future design document, commit CI/audit evidence, or edit excluded paths.

proposedContract.examplesAre: The proposed string above is one completed response with one handled incident; the rules below are the complete additive result contract.

responseVariants.condition: Factory Session is running; --dry-run selects the status literal.
responseVariants.fields: Every current running-response field and MovedRecord/SkippedRecord shape is preserved exactly, plus incidents: IncidentDiagnostic[] and escalations: EscalationDiagnostic[].
responseVariants.dryRunRule: The arrays report bounded classifications or would-be stable actions only; --dry-run performs no Work Request, Factory Event append, or move.

responseVariants.fields: Every current factory-not-running field is preserved exactly, plus incidents: [] and escalations: []. No Work list is inspected and no action is attempted.

proposedContract.preservedRecords: moved and skipped retain the exact current record fields, reason literals, ordering, and optional unfinishedChildren behavior.

fieldRules.fingerprint: 64 lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 characters over sessionId|workId|workGeneration|failureCategory|causalEvidence; sweep timestamps, ticks, and attempts are excluded
fieldRules.causalEvidence: non-empty bounded normalized reference, max 1024 characters
fieldRules.classification: one of recoverable, permanent, scope_or_plan_failure, external_blocker, unknown
fieldRules.disposition: one of untriaged, correction-in-progress, externally-blocked, verified-resolved
fieldRules.action: one of none, discovery_prerequisite, escalation, orphan_repair
fieldRules.evidence: 1–16 objects, each with non-empty kind (max 64), reference (max 512), and summary (max 1024)

requiredFields.fingerprint: 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters matching the incident
requiredFields.actionRequestId: stable accepted Work Request identity, max 180 characters

responseRules: Successful completed and dry-run responses always include both arrays; either may be empty.
A non-running skipped response always includes both arrays as empty because no incident source was inspected.

Malformed or contradictory incident metadata fails closed before an action: no guessed diagnostic, Work Request, retry, Factory Event, or move; if the public read itself fails, the current ReconcileError stdout/stderr/exit contract applies.
A lost action/event response is reread by stable identity; accepted readback is reported once, while uncertain readback is a structured blocker and creates no further action.
proposedContract.ownership: Automations owns diagnostic classification; Recordings owns canonical event append/replay/latest projection; Work and Factory Runtime own Work/action controls; the script only renders bounded diagnostics.
proposedContract.validation: Readers validate arrays and exact record shapes before a writer emits them; same-ID payload conflicts and invalid fields fail closed.
proposedContract.migration: No existing output, Work state, recording, or event is backfilled or rewritten. Existing consumers must tolerate/handle the additive arrays before emission.
proposedContract.rollback: Stop the new diagnostic writer and return to the current reconciler read/move output; preserve all existing fields, failed Work, Factory Events, and replay inputs.

contractChanges.compatibility: sessionId, server, status, reason, moved, skipped, every existing record field, reason literal, flag, public read, move, stderr, and exit behavior remain unchanged. incidents and escalations are additive bounded diagnostics on every successful JSON variant only; the diagnostic is not a second queue or lifecycle store. Reader-before-writer deployment is required.
contractChanges.ownership: Automations owns classification; Recordings owns the canonical event projection; Work/Factory Runtime owns public actions; the reconciler only renders the diagnostic result.
contractChanges.validation: Validate the complete response union, bounded diagnostic fields, stable IDs, exact same-ID payload equality, and fail-closed malformed/partial-read behavior in the future policy/contract lanes.
contractChanges.migration: No migration or historical backfill; old JSON responses remain valid and replay without incident facts.
contractChanges.rollback: Disable diagnostic emission and retain the current read/move response, all Factory Events, failed Work, and replay inputs; do not retry or rewrite Work.

inheritedRules.normalization: Trim values, lowercase ASCII identifiers, reject empty/control-character/pipe values, and exclude sweep timestamps, ticks, and Worker Session attempts.
handled: Owned correction-in-progress with nonterminal corrective Work and a future check
Named external hold before its deadline
actionable: Same causal failure after a new correction revision
inheritedRules.canonicalState: Retain every Factory Event and failed Work; derive only the latest-by-fingerprint eligibility projection. No filesystem marker or second queue is correctness state.

caseMatrix.given: A required capability has no bounded public operation or directly cited symbol.
caseMatrix.then: DISCOVERY_REQUIRED; 0 Work Requests, 0 retries, 0 events, 0 moves; return capability, owner, dependency, witness, smallest exit, and stable prerequisite ID.
caseMatrix.observer: Controlled result fields and public request count; existing Work/history remain unchanged.

caseMatrix.given: LA-06 requires InferenceOutput.Artifact, InvocationProtocolResponse exposes only Text/Usage, and localai-project-v1 is immutable for this slice.
caseMatrix.then: CONTRADICTION; 0 duplicate Work Requests, 0 retries, 0 events, 0 moves; name exact boundaries and the allowed discovery/design exit.
caseMatrix.observer: LocalAI event, Worker Session, and Work lineage; failed/corrective/recovery Work remains visible.

caseMatrix.given: A routine criterion is covered by existing public Work, Factory Event, and Worker Session reads and has a permitted design change.
caseMatrix.when: The preflight evaluates the bounded slice.
caseMatrix.then: ADMIT_BOUNDED_SLICE; 0 approval requests, 0 retries, 0 incident events, 0 moves; emit capability/witness map.
caseMatrix.observer: Capability, permitted change, dependency, owner, witness, and no HUMAN_APPROVAL request.

caseMatrix.given: A fingerprint is correction-in-progress with owned nonterminal corrective Work and future check.
caseMatrix.when: The first unchanged eligibility pass runs.
caseMatrix.then: HANDLED; 0 Astra requests, 0 retries, 0 new events, 0 moves.
caseMatrix.observer: Latest projection and failed Work read; history remains visible.

caseMatrix.given: M-04 evidence is unchanged on a second tick.
caseMatrix.then: Exact M-04 no-op counts; no timestamp-derived identity or new event.
caseMatrix.observer: Fingerprint, action/event counts, and historical failure.

caseMatrix.given: M-04 projection is reconstructed after restart/replay.
caseMatrix.when: The next pass checks handled state.
caseMatrix.then: Same projection; 0 new Astra requests, retries, events, or moves.
caseMatrix.observer: Public event replay and Work history equal pre-replay facts.

caseMatrix.given: Complete unowned/untriaged failure evidence has a valid causal witness.
caseMatrix.then: One stable revision-scoped escalation request and 1 matching disposition event; unchanged repeat is 0/0/0/0.
caseMatrix.observer: Public Work request and Factory Event IDs; failed Work and prior evidence remain.

caseMatrix.given: A named external hold is overdue.
caseMatrix.then: One stable escalation request and 1 event; no failed-Work retry or move; repeat is a no-op.
caseMatrix.observer: Escalation/hold deadline, event, and Work history.

caseMatrix.given: The same causal failure remains after a recorded correction revision.
caseMatrix.then: One new revision-scoped escalation request and 1 event; prior correction/history are retained.
caseMatrix.observer: Distinct revision-scoped IDs and complete event/Work history.

caseMatrix.given: A named external hold has a future deadline.
caseMatrix.observer: Latest disposition and hold remain visible.

caseMatrix.given: Captured Work generation differs from current public generation.
caseMatrix.observer: Current Work generation and failed history are unchanged.

caseMatrix.given: An active Worker Session exists, including an active observation without Work identity.
caseMatrix.observer: Worker Session read and Work state show no mutation.

caseMatrix.given: Factory Session is not RUNNING or a required public read is invalid.
caseMatrix.observer: Session/read error retained; no guessed mutation or history loss.

caseMatrix.given: The same action request or event ID is already visible with an equivalent payload.
caseMatrix.then: ALREADY_RECORDED; 0 new requests, 0 new events, 0 retries, 0 moves.
caseMatrix.observer: Public IDs and exact payload equality; retained event/history stay intact.

caseMatrix.given: An action or event response is lost.
caseMatrix.when: The next pass rereads public facts.
caseMatrix.then: Accepted readback reuses identity with 0 duplicate requests/events; otherwise PARTIAL_WRITE_UNCERTAIN with 0 further actions.
caseMatrix.observer: Public Work/Event readback and structured blocker; no deletion or retry.

caseMatrix.given: Metadata is missing, malformed, contradictory, or fingerprint-invalid.
caseMatrix.then: Validation rejects/fails closed; 0 requests, 0 events, 0 retries, 0 moves.
caseMatrix.observer: Structured validation reason; Work, failed history, and unrelated active Work remain.

caseMatrix.given: Waiting parent has matching generation, no same-name cycle, no active Worker Session, valid readiness, and no duplicate.
caseMatrix.then: Exactly 1 stable move, 1 WORK_STATE_CHANGE, and 1 successful next-dispatch readback; no failed-Work retry.
caseMatrix.observer: Public Work target/dispatch readback; failed and unrelated Work remain visible.

caseMatrix.given: Routine design has no authority, budget, safety, or immutable-contract decision.
caseMatrix.then: Continue autonomously; 0 invented approval requests; escalate only on a real authority/contract/safety/budget decision.
caseMatrix.observer: Review path and request count; no live Factory mutation.

procedure: Record fixture identity, source revision, and baseline request, move, event, retry, failed-Work, handled-visibility, and unrelated-Work counts.
Walk M-01–M-03 and M-18 with a monotonic ten-minute preflight timer; timeout is BLOCKED, never permission to continue.
Walk M-04–M-10 with a deterministic clock across first pass, unchanged second tick, restart/replay, overdue/future hold, and correction revision; record stable IDs and no-op counts.
Walk M-11–M-17 with copied public Work, Session, Worker Session, and event facts; use controlled fake append/action/readback outcomes only at the external-effect boundary.
Compare every result with the matrix; record mismatch as a finding and leave the source fixture and active Factory untouched.

Emit PASS only for observed design properties; emit BLOCKED for unproven runtime/delivery edges with owner, uncertainty, smallest delta, and retest scope.

deliveryProjection.sourceSha256AndBytes: Compute from the exact UTF-8 bytes immediately before delivery and include both values in the generated source object; current measurement is sha256 126facfa560922ab0a0756ee30c97ebb5ac9c2c25ec2409f99dd01b808ed0439 and 98086 bytes.
deliveryProjection.algorithm: Read prd.json as UTF-8 bytes; compute sha256 and byte count; parse JSON; copy only projectionKeys in that order under a source object containing file, sha256, bytes, and the bounded-projection note; serialize with ensure_ascii=false, sort_keys=true, and separators=(',', ':'); assert UTF-8 byte length < 65536; write only the temporary bodyFile; delete it after gh completes.
deliveryProjection.fullSourceRule: The full prd.json remains the immutable handoff input and is not committed or passed directly as --body-file.

futureCommands.delivery: python -m json.tool <task-json> && python -m json.tool prd.json; git diff --check; generate .prd-body.json with deliveryProjection.algorithm; git push; gh pr create --base main --head factory-feasibility-disposition-prerequisite --title factory-feasibility-disposition-prerequisite --body-file .prd-body.json (or gh pr edit <number> --body-file .prd-body.json when the PR already exists); delete .prd-body.json; confirm required CI started on the exact head and stop

qualityBoundaries.securityPrivacy: Bounded normalized keys/references/summaries only; no raw provider output, prompts, credentials, tokens, or transcript bodies; existing Factory authorization remains authoritative.
qualityBoundaries.accessibilityLocalization: No UI/browser/product-copy change in this packet; any future UI must follow repository website and accessibility standards.
qualityBoundaries.performance: Do not broaden the fifteen-minute reconciler into an unmeasured event scan; report event/read/action counts and canary readback latency without inventing a threshold.
qualityBoundaries.cost: 0 provider/model calls, USD 0, 0 download bytes, at most two read-only inspection processes and 256 MiB temporary disk.
